title: Day 6 — Full Slate
_comment: #39 (Phase 2). First post-tutorial day: no new tool, no new page. Rulebook inherited from day_01.json with today's Overseer-Variable flips, same as day 5 — day5_graduation's promised rulebook change is Phase 3's payoff (days 8-11, added_rules/removed_rules), not this day's.
_comment_mix: archetype_mix is authored explicitly (not band-derived) so dark_web:1 is a declared, deterministic slot rather than a statistical maybe — see test_day_06_and_07_guarantee_a_dark_web_slot.
_comment_violations: allowed_violations is omitted on purpose: the per-day whitelist was tutorial scaffolding (#32) pacing which evidence kinds could appear day-by-day. Every kind's revealing tool is already taught by day 5, so dropping the whitelist here matches what synthesize_day already does for every unauthored day beyond the tutorial.

rule_sheet.summary: Same lines in the book as yesterday — but check the severities before you lean on one; at least one of them just moved. No new tool, no new page: you have the full set now, and the whole catalog of things worth checking is fair game, not just the slice each tutorial day let through.
notes: A network of sock-puppet accounts under one handle is a deny.
A handle that apes a listed organisation's handle is a flag on its own — corroborate before denying.
Accounts all created within days of each other, built for this and nothing else, is a deny. That's a burner identity.
A handle matching a known threat-forum account is a deny, full stop.
Traffic that never crosses the brute-force line but never lets up either is a deny — it will not flag itself. You have to go looking.
